card.name: Unusual punctuation marks replacing commas and hyphens
card.fires_on: Rare look-alike punctuation such as ‚ (low quote used as a comma), ‑ (non-breaking hyphen) and › (angle quote) in place of a plain comma, hyphen or apostrophe. Seen in drug-label text, often after a clause like "Prior to use".

modes.label: Low quote as comma
modes.description: The character ‚ stands in for a comma after an introductory phrase or clause.
modes.example: Prior to use<<‚>> remove the carton from the refrigerator (

modes.label: Non-breaking hyphen
modes.description: The character ‑ appears inside a hyphenated compound.
modes.example: use effective non<<‑>>hormonal contraception during treatment with ID

modes.label: Angle quote as apostrophe or separator
modes.description: The character › appears where an apostrophe or a breadcrumb separator would normally be.
